name: limpet
brief: Limpet: a rock mimic about 0.8 m across that clings to asteroids, camouflaged as a lump of rock; it fires a fleshy tendril from its snout to reel prey in, then rides them, biting. A low, lumpy, faceted dome of grey-brown rock that is, on a closer look, overlapping plates: three on its back (plate_l, plate_r, plate_rear) lift when it hunts, showing soft dark flesh under them. Eight glistening purple-red foot lobes ripple round the base rim; a fleshy siphon snout pitches under the shell's front edge; a cluster of pale-green glowing eye pits on the front edge. Origin on the surface it clings to, centred under it. Weak spot: a hot-magenta sac under the gap between the back plates, a thin crack when they're closed, exposed when they lift about 25 degrees.
